what: Website-fingerprinting resistance of the constant-rate WireGuard + DAITA carrier wrapped in the HTTP/3 cloak, measured with tools/daita_lab.py and tools/wf_attack.py across 30 synthetic sites (300 page loads per rate class), and protocol identification with nDPI 4.2 (ndpiReader) and TShark 4.4.19

setup.chain: 2 hops in network namespaces (client, relay, exit, destination), constant cells on every hop
setup.latency: netem 10 ms at each end of every link: about 60 ms round trip end to end
setup.workload: 30 synthetic sites (main document plus 3-28 objects, 77-594 KB), 10 loads each in shuffled order (300 loads per run), 2 parallel connections, sizes +-15% and ~10% of objects skipped per load, 5 s between loads, 20 s initial idle capture
setup.attack: k-FP-style features plus CUMUL, 500-tree random forest, stratified 5-fold cross-validation; closed world, 30 sites, random chance = 0.033 (3.3%)

views.carrier: client <-> first hop: constant-rate WireGuard + DAITA inside HTTP/3 cloak on UDP 443, what the client's ISP sees
views.inner link: first hop <-> exit: QUIC with constant cells, no DAITA constant-rate stream (the same loads, as a baseline)

windows.fixed 6 s: every load gets the same 6 s from its true start: the realistic view of a continuous constant-rate stream that emits no start or end marker on the wire
windows.true end + 3 s: each load cut at its true end + 3 s: an oracle-assisted view where the attacker is told the exact timestamp every page finished loading

metered.grid: 20 ms x 1 slot (50 pps per direction)

fast.grid: 2 ms x 8 staggered slots (4,000 pps per direction)

accuracy_30_sites.reading: Under the fixed 6 s window (no external page-completion oracle), both metered (3.3%) and fast (1.7%) are at or below the 3.3% random-chance floor for 30 sites, whereas the unshaped inner link scores 27.0% (metered pacing) and 74.7% (fast pacing). Even when an external oracle tells the classifier the exact instant each page finished loading (true end + 3 s), carrier accuracy drops from 42.7-81.3% on the inner link to 20.0-21.3% (driven by oracle duration alone).

protocol_identification.carrier_udp_primary: nDPI 4.2: QUIC (proto 188), category Web - the WireGuard+DAITA carrier rides inside the HTTP/3 cloak on UDP 443, so it is not identified as a VPN
protocol_identification.carrier_tcp_fallback: TLS 1.3 on TCP 443 (ALPN http/1.1) with constant 1420-byte cells when UDP 443 is blocked; automatic 2 s fallback and 10 s QUIC recovery probes
protocol_identification.active_probing_origin: Unauthenticated HTTP/3 (UDP 443) and HTTPS (TCP 443) probes receive a 200 OK static HTML5 status page with Alt-Svc: h3=":443"; ma=86400 and forward nothing to the carrier
protocol_identification.between_hops: nDPI: QUIC, category Web, ALPN h3, no hostname
protocol_identification.caveat: the outer QUIC/TLS handshake uses standard rustls/quinn parameters rather than a Chrome uTLS fingerprint, and the certificate is self-signed and SPKI-pinned

padding_and_shaping.carrier_data_packets: every WireGuard packet inside the cloak travels as a 1420-byte outer payload (1448-byte IPv4 packet on the wire)
padding_and_shaping.multi_slot_staggering: MachineTimers::decoy_expiry staggers multi-slot initial deadlines evenly across the 2 ms grid tick ((timeout * idx) / slots), eliminating multi-slot burst quantization and bringing fast fixed-window WF accuracy to 1.7% (chance 3.3%)

http3_and_tcp_camouflage.what: advanced-vpn-cloak carries each WireGuard datagram as a 1420-byte QUIC DATAGRAM frame on UDP 443 (or a 1420-byte TCP/TLS 1.3 cell on TCP 443 when UDP is blocked), authenticated by a 32-byte TLS 1.3 exporter HMAC (EXPORTER-advanced-vpn-cloak)
http3_and_tcp_camouflage.fails_closed: the cloak requires an underlay IPv4 MTU >= 1448; below that the client refuses to connect and keeps the kill switch
http3_and_tcp_camouflage.roaming: changing the client's address mid-transfer is survived: the cloak reconnects and the carrier keepalive re-learns the address
http3_and_tcp_camouflage.liveness_guard: vendor/gotatun flushes the strict-blocking delay queue if real packets sit behind active blocking with no decoy drain for 3 s, preventing start-outage stalls
